objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with small, non-pruritic bumps on the left thigh and general malaise.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I’ve noticed small, non-itchy bumps on my left thigh for about three weeks. I’ve also been feeling tired and generally unwell for a few months. I’m not on any medications, and I do smoke and use intravenous street drugs.
Have you had any fevers, chills, or night sweats during these past few months?
“No, I haven’t had fevers, chills, or night sweats. I’ve just been feeling fatigued and generally unwell, and the bumps on my left thigh have been there for about three weeks.”
Are the bumps painful to touch, and do they have any central dimple or umbilication?
“No, they aren’t painful to touch, and I haven’t noticed any central dimple or umbilication—just small, non-itchy bumps on my left thigh.”
What color are the bumps—are they red, purple, skin-colored, or another color, and approximately how big are they?
They look skin-colored to slightly pink, not bright red or purple, and they’re small—about a few millimeters each.
Do you inject drugs into your left thigh, or have you noticed any similar bumps, sores, or rashes on your palms, soles, or mouth?
I don’t specifically inject into my left thigh, but I do use intravenous street drugs in general. I haven’t noticed any similar bumps, sores, or rashes on my palms, soles, or in my mouth.
Have you experienced any unintentional weight loss over these past few months?
“No, I haven’t had any unintentional weight loss. I’ve mainly just been dealing with fatigue and feeling generally unwell, along with those small non-itchy bumps on my left thigh.”
Have you noticed any swollen lymph nodes in your neck, armpits, or groin?
“I haven’t noticed any swollen lymph nodes in my neck, armpits, or groin, but I do feel generally unwell and tired.”
Have you ever been tested for HIV, hepatitis C, or other blood-borne infections, or received a diagnosis of any of these conditions?

“I haven’t been tested for HIV or hepatitis C recently, and I’ve never received a diagnosis of any blood-borne infection. I’m open to getting tested, given the fatigue, feeling unwell, and these bumps.”
Are the bumps increasing in number, and do they have a smooth surface or a rough, sandpaper-like texture?
“I think the bumps have been slowly increasing in number over the past few weeks, and they feel smooth rather than rough or sandpaper-like.”
Do the bumps blanch (turn white) when you press on them with a finger, or do they stay the same color?
Patient: “When I press on them, they seem to blanch and turn lighter, then they go back to their usual skin-colored to slightly pink appearance afterward.”
Do the bumps bleed easily if you scratch or bump them?

“No, they don’t seem to bleed easily if I scratch or bump them—they just look about the same and don’t ulcerate or bleed. I mainly notice them as small, non-itchy, skin-colored to slightly pink bumps that blanch when pressed.”
Have you noticed any yellowing of your eyes or skin, dark urine, or pain in your upper right abdomen?

“No, I haven’t noticed any yellowing of my eyes or skin, dark urine, or pain in my upper right abdomen. It’s mainly just the fatigue and feeling generally unwell, along with the slowly increasing small, non-itchy bumps on my left thigh.”
[DDX] HIV infection (with cutaneous manifestation), Secondary syphilis, Molluscum contagiosum (possibly indicating underlying immunosuppression), Acute hepatitis C infection, Cutaneous cryptococcosis
